format.rule: isAppend(base, next): next.steps is longer than base.steps; next.steps[i] equals base.steps[i] as a JSON value for every i below base.steps.count (ids, sub-steps and unknown keys included); every top-level key other than steps is present in both or absent in both, with equal values. JSON value equality ignores key order and white space. Bodies are compared as parsed JSON, never as decoded models. appendedSince(history, base): every revision from base + 1 to the newest is isAppend of the one before it.
format.check: {name, note, kind: "check", base, next, expect: {append}}. base and next are body texts, exactly as a Pond could serve them (ids present). append is isAppend(base, next).
format.chain: {name, note, kind: "chain", revisions: [{rev, prev, at, reason, body, hash}...], accepted, tamper?: {rev}, expect: {state, problem?, pondAdvances}}. body is the canonical text; hash is "hook-rev-v1" US rev US prev US at US reason US body (US = U+001F, SHA-256, lowercase hex). accepted is the revision the owner accepted on this device. tamper names the revision whose served hash has one hex digit flipped (the hashes after it are left as computed). state: current (the newest revision is accepted, or every revision after accepted is an append), pending (a revision after accepted is not an append), historyChanged (the history check fails; problem as in history-vectors.json). pondAdvances is the Pond's call on its own (untampered) store, made as each revision k after accepted arrives: k becomes the Pond's accepted revision when accepted == k - 1 and isAppend(k - 1, k). pondAdvances is true when that carries the accepted revision to the newest, N.
format.append: {name, note, kind: "append", current, used, rev, request: {note, steps}, expect}. current is the newest revision's body (an object, ids present); used is every step id of every earlier revision; rev is the revision the append would become; request is the append call's body. Steps without an id get r<rev>-<n>, n counting steps and sub-steps without an id in document order and skipping any id in use, as an amendment numbers them. expect is {ok: true, body, added: [{id, path}]} with body the canonical text of current with the steps appended, and path the 1-based top-level step number as a string, or {ok: false, status, error, details}. Detail paths name the request (steps[0] is the request's first step), except a limit on the whole result, which names the result as the post rules do.
